subject: Biology
central_question: How do pathogens, immune responses, cancer, HIV and substance abuse affect human health, and how can their risks be prevented or controlled?
in_scope_units: Meaning of health, determinants of health and infectious versus non-infectious disease.
Common bacterial, viral, protozoan, helminthic and fungal diseases in humans and their prevention.
Innate and acquired immunity, antibodies, lymphocytes and immune memory.
Active and passive immunity, vaccination, allergy, autoimmunity and lymphoid organs.
HIV transmission, replication, immune deficiency, diagnosis and prevention of AIDS.
Cancer, malignant transformation, metastasis, detection and treatment.
Opioids, cannabinoids, coca alkaloids, alcohol and tobacco abuse, dependence, effects and prevention.
banned_topics: Detailed microbial industrial applications from Microbes in Human Welfare.
Detailed recombinant DNA tools and vaccine manufacturing processes from biotechnology chapters.
Complete pharmacology or clinical treatment protocols beyond the NCERT chapter.

known_pitfalls.claim: Health means only the absence of disease.
known_pitfalls.correction: Health is a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, influenced by genetic factors, infections and lifestyle.

known_pitfalls.claim: Antibiotics can cure common cold and all other infections.
known_pitfalls.correction: Common cold is caused by rhinoviruses; antibiotics act against susceptible bacteria, not viruses.

known_pitfalls.claim: Acquired immunity is non-specific and has no memory.
known_pitfalls.correction: Acquired immunity is pathogen-specific and is characterised by memory, producing a stronger secondary response.

known_pitfalls.claim: HIV spreads through ordinary social contact or mosquito bites.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter lists sexual contact, contaminated blood, shared infected needles and mother-to-child transmission; casual contact and mosquito transmission are not listed routes.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every tumour is malignant and metastatic.
known_pitfalls.correction: Benign tumours remain localised, while malignant tumours invade tissues and may spread through metastasis.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Exercise 3 to compare transmission of amoebiasis, malaria, ascariasis and pneumonia.
Use NCERT Exercise 8 to differentiate innate/acquired and active/passive immunity.
Use NCERT Exercises 10-11 to trace HIV transmission and immune-system damage.
Use NCERT Exercises 12-13 to distinguish cancer cells and explain metastasis.
Use NCERT Exercises 14-17 to analyse harmful effects, peer influence, dependence and prevention of drug and alcohol abuse.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end-of-chapter Exercises are numbered 1 to 17 and cover public health, transmission, immunity, AIDS, cancer and substance abuse.
